# Exact V7 descriptor proof from the delivered R32 epoch

The original V7 descriptor test is present byte-for-byte in the published R32
commit `ce8915ab8a37cf6a180c60195e7f39abcecf28cc`, tree
`b9bc82618a44c8435d230642ceafbe1657f11247`. An untouched replay in that tree
passed the exact case, including all three historical hashes, counts, the
one controlled route addition, and its actual profile-based ground contacts.
The missing `aspect()` call on today's mixed-epoch material stub is **not**
a reason to relax those historical output assertions or any current supports.

The archive contains 186 original executable/data members, not descriptors,
images, models, a replacement controller, or a copy of the entire checkout.
72 directly or transitively imported/read immutable fixture files already
exist in this repository; the runner copies them into the private old tree
only after matching the published original Git blob ID, SHA-256 and size.
The manifest binds all 258 members, the archive, the R32 commit/tree, and the
original callback bytes. All runtime/data sources come from the archive. The
only installed dependencies used are Three and Playwright/-core with the
original lockfile identities. Playwright is imported by an original test
helper; no browser is started.

The fixed-route child invokes original `tests/stepwalk.cjs` with `DUMP=1` and
constructs the actual old terrace approach geometry. The exact unmodified
parent callback separately builds the seven-zone R32 CPU collision world and
uses `buildAutoRoutes` for the old auto-route invariants. This split prevents
substituting a waypoint capture or accepting a transcript without running
all assertions. The runner requires the only selected original case to
pass, with no skips/cancellations/todos, and cleans up the private tree.

Unlike same-process virtual-module readers, this replay preserves real
historical file URLs, relative JSON scans, and the fixed-route subprocess
working directory. It is an integrity boundary for trusted commit bytes,
not a sandbox for running untrusted code. The contemporary tests still use
the registered current world and unchanged physics; the separate current
selector assertion only checks the Zhaode profile row, not old route counts.
